doc.title: Putter Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 27, 2024

title: Monk's humor on stage and in conversation
summary: Stories of Monk dancing during sets, the heckling lady and the remark 'God is my slave'.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: You passed the audition. Did he speak to the audience on gigs?

No he didn’t do announcing or anything like that. He — one time he said something and it illustrates his humor. His theme song was “Epistrophy” do you know that song? [scats] And so this one set, this was in San Francisco. Now what I’m going to do is the lady says something and then Monk says it back and to get the thing I’m going to just do it without saying he said/she said. And so you can tell I’ve told this story a number of times. So this set, he would play the head and then he would get up and dance through the whole thing and then sit down and play the thing out. Did that with every tune in the set. And then played the [scats] the theme to go out. And then he stood up to dance again, and the lady says, “Monk, I paid good money to see you.” “Are you blind?” That was the thing. And the entire — the band and the entire audience just went, you know laughed like crazy. It was definitely worth the price of admission you know. And people would say things to him, was he across, you know, going into the gig and such, and people would say

something and he’d answer them. And the things that I thought were amazing other people were offended you know. And one of the things somebody said, “What about God, Thelonious?” “God is my slave!” I thought that was wonderful. “God is my slave.” “Yeah baby.”
It is unique. Yeah. Okay so anyway, sorry.
